This comparison examines the proportion of atrial fibrillation patients who were admitted with an ischemic stroke or a stroke of unknown type and had redeemed a prescription for oral anticoagulation (AK) treatment within 100 days prior to their admission. The data provides a breakdown of this metric across national and regional levels.

Nationally, across [[danmark|Danmark]], 65.5% of these patients (739 out of 1,128) had an active oral anticoagulation prescription before their stroke admission, while 34.5% (389 patients) did not [^src1]. 

At the regional level, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] leads with the highest proportion of patients having redeemed a prescription prior to admission, at 74.3% (168 out of 226 patients) [^src1]. [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] follows with 70.4% (88 out of 125 patients) [^src1]. Conversely, [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] records the lowest proportion, with only 60.3% (120 out of 199 patients) having redeemed a prescription within the 100-day window [^src1]. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] also falls noticeably below the national average, with 61.4% (121 out of 197 patients) [^src1]. [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] sits slightly below the national baseline at 63.5% (242 out of 381 patients) [^src1]. 

Because the data is drawn from a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends can be established regarding changes in pre-admission anticoagulation rates over time. Region Syddanmark stands out as a positive outlier, significantly outperforming the national average, while Region Midtjylland and Region Sjælland represent the trailing end of the distribution.
